$comment: The fourth review of the interpolation judgement, judged by both editors alike: an unsigned number is not a kotlin.Number, so interpolate refuses it where only a number is let in; markup a Kotlin template writes into interpolate's format is read as format; `<$name` is a tag only when what follows the template could go on with one; and markup held as a String in a val or in a joinToString of Html.

cases.name: a UInt in data-signals: interpolate always throws, a UInt is not a Number
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(u: UInt) = interpolate("""

""", u)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: u is an unsigned number, which is not a kotlin.Number, and it lands in data-signals, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, where only a number or a boolean is let in. Convert it with toLong() first.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(u: UInt) = interpolate("""

""", u.toLong())

cases.name: a ULong in style: interpolate always throws
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(w: ULong) = interpolate("""

""", w)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: w is an unsigned number, which is not a kotlin.Number, and it lands in style, which is read as CSS, where only a number is let in. Convert it with toLong() first.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(w: ULong) = interpolate("""

""", w.toLong())

cases.name: an unsigned literal in data-signals: interpolate always throws
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f() = interpolate("""

""", 5u)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: 5u is an unsigned number, which is not a kotlin.Number, and it lands in data-signals, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, where only a number or a boolean is let in. Convert it with toLong() first.

cases.name: a UInt written by Kotlin: digits, but interpolate would refuse it in data-signals and style
cases.source:
fun f(u: UInt) = """

$u

"""

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${u} into data-signals as digits, which is safe there, but it is an unsigned number, which interpolate refuses there: it is not a kotlin.Number. Convert it with toLong() if you build this with interpolate.

Kotlin writes ${u} into style as digits, which is safe there, but it is an unsigned number, which interpolate refuses there: it is not a kotlin.Number. Convert it with toLong() if you build this with interpolate.

cases.name: a Number written by Kotlin is safe in data-signals and style
cases.source:

$n

"""

cases.name: an Html a Kotlin template writes into the format is read as format

issues.message: Kotlin fills in $inner before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a hole and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s hole and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.

cases.name: an Html in a braced template before a %s hole
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(h: Html, q: String) = interpolate("
${h} %s
", q)

issues.message: Kotlin fills in ${h} before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a hole and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s hole and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(h: Html, q: String) = interpolate("
%s %s
", h, q)

cases.name: a Trusted a Kotlin template writes into the format is read as format
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Trusted fun f(x: String) = interpolate("
${Trusted(x)}
")

issues.message: Kotlin fills in ${Trusted(x)} before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a hole and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s hole and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Trusted fun f(x: String) = interpolate("
%s
", Trusted(x))

cases.name: markup held as a String a Kotlin template writes into the format: no %s fix, which would escape it
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.* fun f(q: String) = interpolate("
${elements { b { +q } }}
")

issues.message: Kotlin fills in ${elements { b { +q } }} before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a hole and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s hole and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.

cases.name: <$name before a backslash is a search pattern, not a tag
cases.source: fun f(tagg: String, html: String) = Regex("<$tagg\\b[^>]*").find(html)

cases.name: <$name at the end of a literal is a search pattern, not a tag
cases.source: fun f(tagg: String, html: String) = html.indexOf("<$tagg")

cases.name: <${name} before another character is not a tag
cases.source: fun f(tagg: String, html: String) = html.indexOf("<${tagg}-x")

cases.name: <$name before a space is a tag
cases.source: fun f(tag: String) = "<$tag class=\"x\">y</$tag>"

cases.name: a val set to elements { } is markup held as a String

issues.message: interpolate escapes e here, so the tags it holds are printed as text: it is markup held as a String. Pass the Html itself, join a list of Html with joinToHtml(), or wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a val set to elements { } is markup in a Kotlin template
a joinToString of a List<Html> is markup held as a String
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(rows: List) = interpolate("
    %s
", rows.joinToString(""))

issues.message: interpolate escapes rows.joinToString("") here, so the tags it holds are printed as text: it is markup held as a String. Pass the Html itself, join a list of Html with joinToHtml(), or wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a joinToString of a List<Html> is markup in a Kotlin template

    ${rows.joinToString("")}
"
